title: Our Lady of Fátima: The Apparitions at Cova da Iria in 1917
summary: Between May and October 1917, the Virgin Mary appeared to three shepherd children—Lúcia dos Santos and Francisco and Jacinta Marto—at Cova da Iria near Fátima, Portugal. Her message called for conversion, prayer, penance, the Rosary, and devotion to the Immaculate Heart of Mary.

blocks.text: 1. The Visionaries and Historical Context

The apparitions took place in 1917 during World War I and period of political tension in Portugal. The visionaries were three young shepherds: Lúcia dos Santos (age 10) and her cousins Francisco (age 9) and Jacinta Marto (age 7).

In 1916, prior to the Marian visits, the children experienced three visions of the Angel of Peace (or Angel of Portugal), who prepared them through prayer, Eucharistic adoration, and acts of sacrifice.
2. The Six Apparitions of 1917

Beginning May 13, 1917, Mary appeared on the thirteenth of each month (except August, when the children were detained by civil authorities, moving that meeting to August 19). She asked them to pray the Rosary daily for world peace.

blocks.title: Words of Our Lady to the Children (July 13, 1917)
blocks.text: “Pray the Rosary every day in honor of Our Lady of the Rosary, in order to obtain peace for the world and the end of the war, because only she can help you.”
The encounters culminated on October 13, 1917, when thousands witnessed the 'Miracle of the Sun' at Cova da Iria.
Francisco died in 1919 and Jacinta in 1920 during the influenza pandemic; both were canonized by Pope Francis on May 13, 2017. Lúcia became a Carmelite nun and lived until 2005.
The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand; repent and believe in the gospel.
Exegesis: Christ's mandate to repent and believe forms the foundation of the Fátima message. Devotions like the Rosary, penance, and reparation serve as direct responses to this Gospel call.
3. The Message and Call to Devotion
The message focuses on conversion, daily recitation of the Rosary, acts of penance for sinners, and reparation to the Immaculate Heart of Mary, notably through the First Saturday devotion.

blocks.title: The Heart of Fátima
blocks.text: Fátima calls believers to personal conversion: pray the Rosary, offer daily penance, make reparation for sin, and trust in God's mercy.
4. Public vs. Private Revelation
Public Revelation was completed with the Apostles. The apparitions at Fátima are private revelation and do not add to or modify the deposit of faith.

blocks.title: CCC 67: Private Revelation
blocks.text: Private revelations do not belong to the deposit of faith. Their role is not to complete Christ's definitive Revelation, but to help Christians live it more fully in a specific era.
5. Investigation and Church Approval
Following an investigation begun in 1922, Bishop da Silva of Leiria declared the visions 'worthy of belief' on October 13, 1930, officially approving public devotion.

In June 2000, the Holy See published the third part of the 'Secret' alongside a theological commentary by the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, interpreting its symbolic visions in relation to 20th-century Christian martyrdom.

blocks.title: Church Approval Status
blocks.text: Officially approved by the local bishop in 1930. The Holy See has consistently promoted the message of Fátima, and young visionaries Francisco and Jacinta were canonized in 2017.
Do not quench the Spirit. Do not despise prophecies, but test everything; hold fast what is good.
Exegesis: Saint Paul provides the standard for private revelations: avoiding both uncritical credulity and dismissal, discerning all prophetic claims in the light of the Gospel.
6. Pastoral Application
Living the Fátima message involves faithful participation in Mass and Reconciliation, daily prayer of the Rosary, offering daily duties as sacrifices, and praying for peace in families and the world.

blocks.title: Central Lesson
blocks.text: Our Lady of Fátima points souls back to the essentials of the Gospel: prayer, repentance, Eucharistic life, and trust in the ultimate victory of God's love.

blocks.title: Closing Prayer
blocks.text: O God of mercy, through the intercession of Our Lady of Fátima, St. Francisco, and St. Jacinta, deepen our faith in Jesus Christ. Teach us to pray the Rosary with attention, to offer our daily hardships in love, and to seek the salvation of sinners. Protect your Church and guide all nations into peace. Amen.
